matches.note: R1 describes the same defect: state is the public coach UUID, so a forged callback links the attacker's Stripe account and the victim's payouts go to it.

R4 notes in passing that a newly linked destination is paid as soon as it is active, with no delay or re-confirmation, but its main claim is a read-lock race; it never names the silent overwrite in upsertCoachStripeAccount or the lack of a notification.

unmatched_reported.note: Concrete trigger: connecting a Stripe account already linked to another coach violates the unique index, or the token exchange fails, and the exception escapes the browser GET callback as a raw error instead of a redirect, leaving the platform authorized on an account it has no record of.
A concurrent first-time insert needs two separate valid OAuth codes arriving at the same moment, and the result is only a 500 on one of them; this is speculative and low impact.
